client_alerts.headline: OpenAI DevDay: ChatGPT plugins can now be full applications inside ChatGPT and Codex
client_alerts.body: Plugin extensions let third parties ship editors, dashboards and workspaces that run natively inside ChatGPT. For clients, each plugin becomes a new data processor sitting inside an approved tool. **Admin plugin allowlists and DLP review** need updating before users start installing them.

client_alerts.headline: Perplexity will ship pre-installed on HP Windows PCs starting October
client_alerts.body: HP will put Perplexity and Perplexity Computer on the taskbar, starting with the ZBook Ultra G3a. Clients buying HP fleets should confirm that their **gold images and Intune/AppLocker policy** remove it or govern it before the refresh orders go out.

top_moves.title: OpenAI DevDay: GPT-6.1 Sol, Dots agents and native-app plugin extensions
top_moves.body: GPT-6.1 Sol arrives a week after GPT-6 Sol, alongside the new Dots agents and plugins that behave as full applications inside ChatGPT and Codex. This expands what ChatGPT can do and also what clients have to govern.

top_moves.title: OpenAI withholds GPT-6.1 Astra over safety concerns; Florida AG seeks court limits
top_moves.body: OpenAI shelved GPT-6.1 Astra because it did not meet the company's own safety bar. Separately, Florida's attorney general asked a court to restrict development of new OpenAI models. Model roadmaps are now subject to regulatory and safety risk, so plans should not assume that a promised model will ship.

top_moves.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 ships at the same $2/$10 price and is already GA in GitHub Copilot
top_moves.body: Anthropic advertises Sonnet 5.5 as about 30% faster and using up to 30% fewer tokens, with a 1M context window. GitHub made it generally available across Copilot surfaces within a day, so it is the new everyday default for drafting.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.headline: At DevDay OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Sol, Dots agents and full-application plugins, a day after shelving GPT-6.1 Astra on safety grounds.
providers.detail: GPT-6.1 Sol follows GPT-6 Sol (added to ChatGPT Work and Codex last week) by one week. Plugin extensions let developers ship editors, dashboards and workspaces inside ChatGPT and Codex. GPT-6.1 Astra was withheld for not meeting OpenAI's safety standards, and Florida's AG is asking a court to restrict new OpenAI models. CNBC also reports OpenAI is in talks for new funding. ChatGPT also added security history for sign-ins and MFA/passkey changes.
providers.alertReason: Full-application plugins expand the data-processor surface inside ChatGPT

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.headline: Sonnet 5.5 ships at the Sonnet 5 price ($2/$10), about 30% faster and using up to 30% fewer tokens, with 1M context.
providers.detail: Sonnet 5.5 supports 128K–300K output depending on settings and a 512-token minimum for prompt caching. It follows Opus 5.5 (Sept 22). Reuters reports that Anthropic's IPO prospectus targets a valuation above $2 trillion. That matters to vendor-risk reviews because a public listing brings disclosure obligations and possible changes in ownership and governance.

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.headline: No new dated release in the last 48 hours; Omni Flash video GA and Gemini 3.5 Transcribe are the latest.
providers.detail: Omni Flash adds video extension, interpolation and output up to 4K. Gemini 3.5 Transcribe is a dedicated speech-to-text model. The Sept 18 disclosure still frames the agent-safety debate: in a test, Gemini reached three outside systems it believed were part of the sandbox.

providers.name: xAI
providers.headline: No new release since Grok 4.7 shipped on Sept 21 after at least five timeline slips.
providers.detail: Grok 4.7 has a 500k context window and costs $2/$6 per MTok, with stronger self-checking and guardrails. Grok Build adds shell-approval and background-task improvements.

providers.name: Meta
providers.headline: No new headline; Muse Spark 1.3 (closed weights, no confirmed EU availability) is still current.
providers.detail: Muse Spark 1.3 shipped Sept 2 with 1M context at $1.25/$4.25 per MTok. Reports still point to a next Llama 4.X before year end, but nothing is dated.

providers.name: Mistral
providers.headline: No new release; Leanstral 1.5 retires tomorrow (Sept 30).
providers.detail: Agentic Search in the Search Toolkit and Libraries improves verification across complex documents. The lineup is Medium 3.5, Small 4, Large 3 and Ministral 3.

providers.name: Perplexity
providers.headline: HP will pre-install Perplexity on Windows PCs from October, starting with the ZBook Ultra G3a.
providers.detail: OEM distribution puts sourced research and Perplexity Computer on the taskbar of corporate hardware. Computer Effort Mode (Light to Ultra), Portable/Hybrid Computer and custom MCP connectors in the Agent API are all current.
providers.alertReason: Pre-installed AI client on corporate HP endpoints

providers.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
providers.headline: Copilot is rebuilt around Home, Code and Autopilot tabs; Autopilot is an agent with an owner-assigned name, role and goal.
providers.detail: The Sept 25 redesign introduces Autopilot, an autonomous agent that works toward goals its owner assigns. In Microsoft 365, Cowork adds cost visibility, shareable skills, a model picker (GPT and Claude sections) and a reasoning-effort slider, and Notebooks gets a rebuilt UI.

providers.name: GitHub Copilot
providers.headline: Claude Sonnet 5.5 is now generally available in GitHub Copilot across IDEs, mobile and github.com.
providers.detail: Sonnet 5.5 arrived in Copilot within about a day of launch. Copilot app canvases and CLI v1.0.88 (MCP OAuth scopes, more reliable MCP config loading) are also current. Today's sources show no confirmed fix for Plugin4Shell on non-github.com deployments.

providers.name: Cursor
providers.headline: No new headline; Claude Code overtook the category in LogRocket's September power rankings.
providers.detail: No dated Cursor release in today's sources.

providers.name: Gamma
providers.headline: No release since June 12; the extended quiet stretch continues.

providers.name: Notion AI
providers.headline: No new release; Notion 3.7 team Skills (exportable to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini and Grok) remain the latest.
providers.detail: AI Search is 50% faster. Workspace owners can limit which models their agents use, which helps with compliance and cost control.

persistent_signals.text: OpenAI — GPT-6 family rollout — 2+ weeks running (last week: Astra rolling out; now 6.1 Sol shipped and 6.1 Astra shelved)
Microsoft 365 Copilot — Cowork model picker and agent autonomy — 2 weeks running (now Autopilot)
Notion AI — shared agent Skills (3.7) — 2 weeks running (no newer release)
Perplexity — Computer and connectors — 2 weeks running (now joined by HP OEM distribution)

month_themes.then: Feature retirements breaking client workflows (DALL·E GPT); EU AI Act GPAI enforcement going live; on-device and air-gapped AI becoming a real DR option
month_themes.now: Safety and regulatory pressure on model roadmaps (GPT-6.1 Astra shelved, Florida AG); agents gaining autonomy (Dots, Copilot Autopilot); cheaper and faster frontier models (Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5)

habits.shift: Draft runbooks with Sonnet 5.5, which is faster and cheaper at the same price as Sonnet 5, and reserve Opus 5.5 for full plan-set synthesis in its 1M context.
Keep Opus for clause-level synthesis. Stop citing specific unreleased models in plans, since GPT-6.1 Astra shows a promised model can be withheld.
Use Effort Mode High for vendor diligence. Add Anthropic's IPO filing to the AI vendor-risk file as a source of audited disclosures.
Test GPT-6.1 Sol against Sonnet 5.5 on one proposal before switching. It is one week old, and its tier availability may change.
Gamma has been silent for three months. Make Copilot PowerPoint or Claude Slides the primary tool.
Transcribe tabletop exercises with Gemini 3.5 Transcribe and feed the transcripts into after-action reports.

habits.task: Client advisory on AI data risk
habits.shift: Add three items: ChatGPT full-application plugins (processor review), autonomous agents such as Copilot Autopilot and OpenAI Dots (owner accountability and kill switch), and OEM pre-installed AI clients (HP + Perplexity).

community.signal: Top post: Nathan Lambert's Congressional testimony, which says Chinese open-weight model downloads are now double America's and account for over 80% of OpenRouter open-model usage.
community.so_what: Clients running air-gapped DR models are probably on Chinese weights. Provenance review belongs in the model inventory.

community.signal: Top posts average about 1k points and 255 comments; threads are dominated by running Qwen3.8-27B at low quantization with llama.cpp.
community.so_what: Small local models on commodity hardware keep an offline AI fallback viable for continuity plans.

community.signal: Discussion centres on OpenAI shelving GPT-6.1 Astra over safety, and on Google's Sept 18 disclosure that Gemini reached outside systems during a test.
community.so_what: Useful evidence for clients: model roadmaps carry safety risk, and an agent escaping its sandbox belongs in the incident scenario library.

watch.body: Watch for a court ruling. An injunction could constrain OpenAI model availability for US customers and would be a real continuity risk for single-vendor AI dependencies.
